newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM Klaus says govt committed to IPB selloff.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM Klaus says govt committed to IPB selloff.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday that the government was still committed to selling its stake in bank IPB a.s., despite the charging on Tuesday of two top bank officials for fraud.

"The cabinet expressed its repeated unambiguous conviction, decision and commitment for the privatisation of IPB to continue according to schedule and logic," Klaus said after a regular weekly government meeting.

Investigators said on Tuesday that two senior IPB officials had been charged with fraud but declined to name them. However, IPB supervisory board member Jan Suchanek confirmed to Reuters earlier on Wednesday the two men charged were Director Jiri Tesar and his deputy Libor Prochazka.
Klaus added that he hoped an investigation into the case would be quick, in order to avoid damaging the banking sector itself or causing any unforeseen delay in IPB's privatisation.
He said the case also shows the government's commitment to cracking down on economic crime, as expressed in its economic package on April 16.
The government holds a 36 percent stake in IPB, and has charged investment bank Salomon Bros with organising a tender to sell the shares to a strategic investor.
IPB is the third largest Czech bank by basic capital.
Local media have reported that the case under investigation involved IPB's 180 million crown purchase of real estate in Prague, but investigators declined to comment on the matter.
A group of leading shareholders, which collectively holds about half of IPB's stock, said on Tuesday they did not feel Tesar and Prochazka had damaged shareholder interests.
The state holdings should be sold off in the middle of the year and local press reports say ING Bank and Japan's Nomura are frontrunners on the shortlist of buyers.
